What's inspected

Six major systems. One structured record.

Findings are organized in the spirit of the TREC REI 7-6 format for clear navigation and consistent condition marking.

I InspectedNI Not InspectedNP Not PresentD Deficient
01 / REI

Structural Systems

Foundation, grading and drainage, roof covering, attic, walls, ceilings, floors, doors and windows.

02 / REI

Electrical Systems

Service entrance, panels, branch circuits, fixtures, receptacles, GFCI and AFCI protection where accessible.

03 / REI

HVAC Systems

Heating and cooling equipment, visible distribution components, thermostats and accessible performance observations.

04 / REI

Plumbing Systems

Visible supply, drains, water heater, fixtures, functional flow and signs of leakage in accessible areas.

05 / REI

Appliances

Installed kitchen, laundry and garage-related appliances included within the inspection scope.

06 / REI

Optional Systems

Applicable items such as irrigation, pools, spas, private water or septic systems when included in the booked scope.

11
The inspection sweet spot

Why timing matters

Your warranty clock does not pause for hidden defects.

Month 11 gives your home time to settle and reveal issues while leaving a practical window to document them before the common one-year deadline.

1

Let the home show its first-year behavior

Seasonal changes and everyday use can expose movement, moisture, drainage, electrical or mechanical concerns.

2

Leave room to act

Waiting until the final days can make inspection, report delivery and builder submission harder to coordinate.

3

Document before costs shift to you

Unreported defects can become more disruptive—and more expensive—after the applicable builder coverage ends.

A little preparation gives the inspector better access.

Homeowner preparation

Make the inspection day count.

Before the appointment, help make important areas safely accessible.

  • ✓Clear access to the attic opening, electrical panel and water heater.
  • ✓Unlock gates, utility spaces and detached structures included in the inspection.
  • ✓Move stored items away from visible plumbing and mechanical equipment.
  • ✓Write down concerns, changes or recurring issues you noticed during the year.
  • ✓Have your closing date and builder warranty documents available for reference.

About

We work for the homeowner—not the builder.

BuilderWarrantyCheck is an independent, Texas-focused building warranty inspection company. Our work centers on the homeowner's first-year warranty window: observing accessible systems, documenting visible concerns and delivering a clear report you can use in your conversation with the builder.

We bring a focused process, plain-English communication and careful photo documentation to one of the most time-sensitive moments in new-home ownership.
